script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. BRIGHT, MINIMALIST APARTMENT - DAY

SARAH (30s, determined) sits at her cluttered desk, staring at her laptop. She clenches her jaw, a line of tension crossing her forehead.

SARAH
(whispering to herself)
I can do this. I'll apply to that marketing position today.

Suddenly, there's a knock at the door. Sarah looks up, startled. She hesitates before getting up to answer it.

INT. APARTMENT ENTRANCE - CONTINUOUS

SARAH opens the door to reveal her former CO-WORKER, MARK (late 30s, smug). He grins as he enters.

MARK
Surprise! I saw your Facebook post about your job search, so I figured I'd stop by and offer my assistance.

Sarah's expression sours. She steps back, closing the door partway.

SARAH
(sarcastically)
Oh, really? How thoughtful of you.

MARK
Look, Sarah, I know we didn't always see eye to eye at the office, but we both know you're talented. I can help you land that marketing job.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Sarah and Mark sit at her kitchen table, poring over her resume and cover letter.

SARAH
I don't know if I can do this, Mark. After all these years in the journalism industry, I'm not sure I have what it takes to start over in marketing.

MARK
(placatingly)
You've got this, Sarah. Just think about all the skills you've gained over the years. Writing, researching, communicating...those are all valuable assets in marketing.

Sarah nods, looking thoughtful.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Sarah and Mark sit at a table, laptops open in front of them. They're surrounded by the hum of other patrons and the aroma of coffee.

SARAH
(excitedly)
I did it! I applied to three marketing positions today.

MARK
(smiling)
That's great news, Sarah. I knew you could do it.

INT. SARAH'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Sarah paces her living room, her phone clutched in her hand. She's waiting for a call or email from a potential employer.

MARK
(entering the apartment)
Hey, you look stressed. Did you hear back from any of those marketing jobs yet?

Sarah shakes her head, frustration etched on her face.

SARAH
No, not yet. It's just...I don't know if I'll ever get a call back. I'm too old, too experienced in the wrong field.

Mark approaches her, placing a hand on her shoulder.

MARK
Don't say that, Sarah. You're never too old to make a change. I believe in you.

INT. INTERVIEW ROOM - DAY

Sarah sits across from a stern-faced INTERVIEWER (50s, unyielding). She answers questions about her qualifications and past experience.

INTERVIEWER
(skeptically)
And why do you want to make the transition from journalism to marketing?

Sarah hesitates, then answers honestly.

SARAH
I've come to realize that my passion lies in strategy and analysis, not just reporting the news. I believe marketing offers me the opportunity to use those skills in a more impactful way.

INT. SARAH'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Sarah receives an email notification on her laptop. She reads the message, her face lighting up with excitement.

SARAH
(to herself, grinning)
I got it! They want to offer me an interview for the marketing position.

Mark enters the room, looking pleased.

MARK
That's amazing news, Sarah! I'm so proud of you.

INT. INTERVIEW ROOM - DAY

Sarah sits across from the interviewer once more, this time more confident and prepared. She answers questions with ease and speaks passionately about her desire to make the career transition.

INTERVIEWER
(impressed)
Ms. Johnson, I think we may have found the candidate we've been looking for. We'd like to offer you the marketing position, subject to reference checks and a background check.

Sarah leaps to her feet, her eyes wide with disbelief.

SARAH
(gratefully)
Thank you so much. I won't let you down.

INT. SARAH'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Sarah sits at her desk, her laptop open to the job offer email. She reads the message, a huge smile on her face.

SARAH
(to herself, happily)
I did it. I'm finally making the transition I've always wanted.

INT. OFFICE - DAY

Months later, Sarah sits at her new desk in her marketing office, surrounded by her co-workers. She looks satisfied and content.

MARK
(entering the office)
Congratulations, Sarah. You've come a long way since that first job application.

Sarah smiles, her eyes filled with gratitude.

SARAH
Thank you, Mark. Your belief in me gave me the confidence I needed to make this change.

MARK
(proudly)
That's what friends are for.

FADE OUT.
